james_acme: hey support — since last deploy our prod service is getting 401 invalid_api_key on every call. SDK from my laptop works fine and curl from my devbox succeeds. only the containerized prod app fails.

james_acme: repro from prod container (masked key):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: ApiKey $API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
> x-request-id: rwd_01H9QK2
{"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"invalid_api_key"}}
```

olivia_support: can you paste how the API_KEY is populated in your container? any secret-manager/ci step that touches it?

james_acme: we fetch it in CI and write to a file, then docker build copies it. the build step runs:
```
export API_KEY="$(gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=redwood-key)"
printf "%s" "$API_KEY" > ./secrets/redwood.key
```
I just cat'ed the file and it looks weird, not like a short token.

sam_engineer: can you show the first bytes (hex) of the file? paste the output of:
```
printf '%s' "$(cat ./secrets/redwood.key)" | head -c 80 | xxd -g 1
```

james_acme: paste from the container:
```
00000000: 2d 2d 2d 2d 2d 42 45 47 49 4e 20 41 47 45 20 45 4e  -- ---BEGIN AGE EN
00000010: 43 52 59 50 54 45 44 20 46 49 4c 45 2d 2d 2d 2d  CRYPTED FILE----
00000020: 2d 0a 61 67 65 2d 65 6e 63 72 79 70 74 65 64 2d  -..age-encrypted-
00000030: 62 6c 6f 62 0a 2d 2d 2d 2d 2d 45 4e 44 20 41 47  lob..-----END AG
```

olivia_support: OK that's the issue — the secret file contains the armored age-encrypted blob (-----BEGIN AGE ENCRYPTED FILE-----...). you never decrypted the secret when building the image, so the app is sending the whole armored file as the key.

sam_engineer: Redwood expects the raw API key string (alphanumeric-ish, ~30-50 chars). An armored blob will always 401. Quick fixes:
- decrypt in CI before writing the file: `age -d secret.age > plain.key` and set that as API_KEY
- or use your secrets manager to provide the plaintext to the build (avoid copying the armored file)

james_acme: thanks — that makes sense. is there a server-side way to return a clearer error for this case so we can detect it earlier in CI?

sam_engineer: we only return generic invalid_api_key for any non-matching credential. Suggest adding a simple client-side sanity check in your pipeline, e.g.:
```
# basic sanity check for obvious armored content
if grep -q "BEGIN AGE" ./secrets/redwood.key; then
  echo "secret looks armored; abort"
  exit 1
fi
# minimal format check (example):
if ! grep -E -q '^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{24,64}$' ./secrets/redwood.key; then
  echo "api key failed basic regex check"
  exit 1
fi
```

olivia_support: also we can add a short KB entry for CI pipelines (how-to detect armored/wrapped secrets). filing a quick doc ticket.
